prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a transparent raster tactical-game wreck sprite atlas, showing ONLY the LIGHT TANK.
Primary request: Generate ONE new square RGBA atlas containing exactly THREE separate complete wreck paintings, in THREE EQUAL HORIZONTAL ROWS and ONE COLUMN. These are three different causal wreck states of the SAME reference vehicle. All vehicles face RIGHT.

Input images are design/style references ONLY, NOT edit targets. Image 1 (tanks-v12.png): use ONLY row 1 for the LIGHT TANK vehicle identity, palette, proportions, roadwheel count, and perspective. Image 2 (ground-wrecks-v14.png): use ONLY row 1, column 1 for the same LIGHT TANK's wreck material treatment, identity, palette, and perspective. Ignore all other cells. Do not reproduce either reference sheet or its background. Produce only the requested model in three rows.
Vehicle identity: Compact box turret, slender gun, compact hull. Preserve exactly FOUR main load-bearing roadwheels along the bottom run, plus the separate raised end sprocket/idler; preserve their spacing and the compact reference wheelbase. The original model must remain instantly recognizable in every damage state.

Scene/backdrop: genuine transparent alpha background. Every empty area, outer margin, and entire gutter must be transparent alpha=0. No painted backdrop or checkerboard pattern.
Style/medium: highly detailed hand-painted 2D SIDE-VIEW realistic pixel tactical-game art matching the inspected references. Fine deliberate pixel clusters, chipped olive armor, readable machinery, nuanced metal edges, bolts, suspension and track links. Strict near-orthographic side camera matching the reference; no isometric or three-quarter view. Neutral readable metal highlights, surviving olive paint, localized charcoal soot, rust and ash. Keep detail readable even in deep structural openings.

Composition and registration: treat the square as three invisible equally sized horizontal panels. Exactly ONE complete wreck per panel. Use exactly the SAME lower-hull footprint, hull length, hull center X, wheelbase, wheel sizes and wheel X locations in every row; identical wheel-ground baseline at the same local height, approximately 80% down each panel. Do not resize the hull between states. Each complete painted state must be self-contained, requiring no anatomical compositing or runtime squashing. Full vehicle including its barrel, displaced turret and every fragment stays inside its own panel. Generous genuine-alpha empty outer margins and gutters; all artwork stays at least 8% of canvas width from left/right edges, with generous clear space above/below each painting. No drawn row lines. Do not stretch vehicle proportions to fill the square.

TOP ROW — ARMOR-PIERCING DEFEAT: localized torn penetration near the turret ring or engine, peeled metal edges and visibly exposed detailed internal parts. Disabled or slack track. Most of the turret remains seated in its original recognizable location. Much olive armor survives, with localized soot around the defeat. Actual structural damage rather than a recolor.

MIDDLE ROW — EXPLOSION DEFEAT: turret dislodged and reclining directly ON/AGAINST ITS OWN HULL, physically supported by it; NOT floating and NOT thrown far away. Open torn turret ring and roof expose layered mechanical interiors, ribs, wires and metal shards. The gun is visibly bent but retains a rightward direction, and the track is slipped. All debris lies immediately under or within the original lower-hull footprint. Preserve the exact same hull size and wheelbase as the top row. Turret stays normal model scale, no huge thrown turret.

BOTTOM ROW — LONG BURN: turret remains recognizably SEATED, with roof and hatches collapsed inward, missing stowage and heat-discolored rust/ash metal. Charred but readable internal ribs, wheels, track details and neutral metal highlights. Surviving olive armor remains. Distinct inward structural collapse and burned material damage, not merely tinted versions of the top or middle row.

Structural requirements: paint detailed actual damage and exposed interiors with depth, readable ribs, torn plate thickness and mechanical parts. No solid black polygons, featureless holes, or all-black silhouettes. Do NOT copy/paste an unchanged intact vehicle and vary only its tint. Do not scatter debris outside the original vehicle's length; keep fragments immediately beneath/within the hull footprint. Wreck states must differ causally while their underlying vehicle anatomy and placement remain registered.

Avoid: background, floor, ground plane, giant shadow, checkerboard image, fire, smoke, text, labels, captions, people, logos, UI, extra vehicles, additional columns, overlapping rows, clipped barrels, floating turrets, oversized detached turrets, or debris extending beyond the original vehicle length. Output exactly one square transparent RGBA image with precisely three separate complete painted wreck states.
